correctness.rationale: For arbitrary nondecreasing positive weights w_j, merging nonnegative coordinates into their sum majorizes the original list, and summation by parts shows Q_w decreases under merging. Coordinatewise |sum x_i|<=sum |x_i| gives Q_w(sum x_i)<=Q_w(disjoint concatenation of |x_i|). Layer cake gives the integral over thresholds of Φ(sum m_i(t)), bounded by the optimal block-count ratio times sum_i Φ(m_i(t)); disjoint constant-height indicators attain any chosen ratio. Since Φ has nondecreasing increments, transferring a unit from a larger to a block at least two smaller cannot increase the sum of Φ, so fixed total S=nm+r is optimized by m,m+1 balanced blocks. For logarithmic weights w_j=1+(log j)^k, Φ(S)/S~(log S)^k; for fixed n the balancing ratio tends to one as S→∞, whereas S=n yields >1, proving the supremum is attained at some finite S (not claiming a uniform computable cutoff). Independently computed n=k=2 witness Φ(10)/(2Φ(5))≈1.6808888313, larger than singleton ratio≈1.2402265070, and checked finite integer-composition optima in the source checker; finite tests do not prove arbitrary n or all weights.
residual_risks: Finite numerical or exhaustive small-parameter checks do not prove unbounded cases; only the reconstructed analytic argument supports universal claims.
